Let
\[
C_\alpha=\{z^8:z\in(\mathbb Z/p^\alpha\mathbb Z)^\times\}
\]
be the octic-unit subgroup. Then
\[
\boxed{
Z_{p,\alpha}
=
\frac{p^{2\alpha-2}(p-1)}{3072}
\left(p-23-(6+12\epsilon_p)x-12(1+\epsilon_p)a\right)
}.
\]

Equivalently,
\[
Z_{p,\alpha}
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{p^{2\alpha-2}(p-1)(p-23+6x)}{3072},
& \epsilon_p=-1,\\[1.1em]
\dfrac{p^{2\alpha-2}(p-1)(p-23-18x-24a)}{3072},
& \epsilon_p=1.
\end{cases}
\]

Here \(x,a,\epsilon_p\) are exactly the integers defined in the problem.

Proof sketch, self-contained: every zero-sum triangle can be written uniquely from an ordered root \(r\) as
\[
\{r,r+u,r+v\},\qquad 3r+u+v=0,
\]
with
\[
u,\ v,\ v-u\in C_\alpha .
\]
Since \(p\ne3\), \(r\) is uniquely determined by \(u,v\). Each unordered triangle is counted \(6\) times, so
\[
Z_{p,\alpha}=\frac16
\#\{(u,v)\in C_\alpha^2:v-u\in C_\alpha\}.
\]

Writing \(v=uq\), this count equals
\[
|C_\alpha|\cdot \#\{q\in C_\alpha:q-1\in C_\alpha\}.
\]
Reduction modulo \(p\) identifies \(C_\alpha\) with the full inverse image of the octic subgroup \(C_1\subset\mathbb F_p^\times\), because raising to the eighth power is an automorphism on the principal units \(1+p\mathbb Z/p^\alpha\mathbb Z\). Hence the count lifts by \(p^{2\alpha-2}\):
\[
\#\{(u,v)\in C_\alpha^2:v-u\in C_\alpha\}
=
p^{2\alpha-2}
\#\{(u,v)\in C_1^2:v-u\in C_1\}.
\]

Let
\[
M=\#\{q\in C_1:q-1\in C_1\}.
\]
Then the mod-\(p\) ordered-pair count is \(\frac{p-1}{8}M\). The standard order-\(8\) character sum evaluation gives
\[
64M=p-23-(6+12\epsilon_p)x-12(1+\epsilon_p)a.
\]
Indeed, using an octic character \(\chi\) on \(\mathbb F_p\),
\[
M=\frac1{64}\sum_{i,j=0}^7 J(\chi^i,\chi^j),
\]
and evaluating the Jacobi sums with
\[
p=x^2+4y^2,\qquad p=a^2+2b^2,
\]
under the stated congruence normalizations yields precisely the displayed value.

Therefore
\[
Z_{p,\alpha}
=
\frac16\cdot p^{2\alpha-2}\cdot \frac{p-1}{8}\cdot
\frac{p-23-(6+12\epsilon_p)x-12(1+\epsilon_p)a}{64},
\]
which simplifies to
\[
\boxed{
Z_{p,\alpha}
=
\frac{p^{2\alpha-2}(p-1)}{3072}
\left(p-23-(6+12\epsilon_p)x-12(1+\epsilon_p)a\right)
}.
\]
